summary.headline: Q2 FY27 revenue rose 59% YoY to INR489 crore, with EBITDA loss narrowing to 3.5% of revenue from 5.2% a year ago.
summary.overview: Revenue from operations reached INR489 crore, up 59% YoY and 11% QoQ, led by RetailerShakti (B2B) at INR429 crore. Gross margin expanded to 8.3% of revenue (from 7.5% a year ago and 7.9% in Q1), and operating expenses fell to 10.8% of revenue from 12.4%. EBITDA loss was INR17.2 crore (-3.5% of revenue), and PAT loss narrowed to INR12.7 crore (-2.6%). Management reiterated 30% compounded growth, lowered its FY30 revenue framing to INR4,900 crore from INR6,000 crore due to a JITO private-label mix shift, and tied the merger completion to a pending SEBI observation letter.

financial_highlights.change: +80 bps YoY (7.5%), +40 bps QoQ (7.9%); gross margin grew 77% YoY
Loss margin improved 170 bps YoY from -5.2%; absolute loss up from -INR16 crore
Loss vs -INR15.4 crore a year ago (loss margin 5% previously)

segments.name: RetailerShakti (B2B)
segments.commentary: Revenue about INR429 crore in Q2, up 60% YoY and 18% QoQ; serves roughly 80,000 retail pharmacies.

segments.name: SastaSundar (B2C)
segments.commentary: Revenue INR55 crore, up 39% YoY; grown for six consecutive quarters from INR32 crore in Q1 FY26. Management says 76% of its business is from Tier 2/3 India.

segments.name: Diagnostics
segments.commentary: Revenue about INR0.8 crore in the quarter.

segments.name: JITO private label
segments.commentary: Cumulative sales INR2.2 crore in the quarter at about 60% gross margin, up about 170% vs Q1 on a very low base; 52 franchise outlets live, 81 in pipeline (analyst cited 80), over 1,000 healthcare SKUs.

guidance_outlook: Management targets about 30% compounded revenue growth; frames the model at roughly 30% with quarterly variation. Also cited IPM growth of 12% implying 18% company growth.
Gross margin path: 8.5-8.6% achieved currently, 9-10% in FY27-28, 10-11% in FY28-29; management said this is a range, not formal guidance.

Revised FY29-30 targets: total revenue INR4,900 crore (from INR6,000 crore), with RetailerShakti INR4,000 crore and SastaSundar about INR900 crore (from INR2,000 crore); JITO to contribute 13% of revenue.
EBITDA target for FY29-30 now above the earlier 5-6% range, per management, due to JITO gross margin; EBITDA loss expected to close via about 2% gross margin expansion and 2% opex reduction.
JITO revenue expected at INR6-10 crore next quarter (INR2-3.5 crore per month).
capex_capacity: Fulfillment centres operating: three (Baruipur WB, Assam, Noida). West Bengal centre fully automated for about 18 months of growth; Noida upgraded to a larger warehouse with double capacity; Guwahati upgraded for about 3 years.
Smaller 20,000 sq ft warehouses in Ranchi, Patna and Bhubaneswar; sign-ups under way, about 6 months before operations.

Larger facilities planned: 1.2 lakh sq ft West Bengal (after 3 years), 75,000 sq ft Guwahati, 80,000 sq ft each Lucknow and Udaipur, and 1.2 lakh sq ft Patna and Bhubaneswar in second phases; total additional about 5.95 lakh sq ft. Udaipur first, in about 18 months; plinth area complete.
Warehouses are a mix of leased and owned land; land acquired via state MOUs at concession rates.
demand_pricing: Over 76% of SastaSundar and 66% of RetailerShakti revenue from Tier 2/3 India; 90% of orders delivered within 24 hours.
Company sells on cash with no credit risk; over 90% of purchases made directly from pharma companies through authorised channels.
Management said credit-based NBFC/bank financing for retailers has seen slow adoption, despite partnerships with two national banks.
Management expects gross margin levers from JITO private label, volume, device/OTC/nutrition mix, and data and logistics monetisation (about 1% of gross margin from data and advertising).
Management said a 50-100 bps annual gross margin expansion is achievable, which it described as a conservative assumption.
Retailers' conference planned for around January with about 10,000 pharmacy retailers.

qa_highlights.question: What are the advantages of large distributors versus small ones in margin and cost terms?
qa_highlights.answer: Management cited bulk-purchase discounts from pharma companies, lower per-unit operating cost at higher throughput, and diversification across markets; no quantification given.

qa_highlights.question: Will the company partner with NBFCs or banks to offer retailer working-capital credit?
qa_highlights.answer: Two national banks and NBFCs are partnered, but adoption is slow due to KYC and documentation; the company says it is ready to fund retailers itself once adoption starts.

qa_highlights.question: How do Healthbuddy franchisees earn margin, and how are orders fulfilled?
qa_highlights.answer: Healthbuddy partners get about 6-7% of sales (3% cost, 4% retention); normal medicine ships from central fulfilment centres, while JITO products are stocked at some stores on a trial basis.

qa_highlights.question: How equipped is infrastructure, and what incremental cost is needed?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said incremental cost is not reportable as the cost base is centralised; it cited incremental cost over EBITDA loss at about 27-28%, recoverable in 3-4 years.

qa_highlights.question: What are the gross margin levers and when will 10% be reached?
qa_highlights.answer: Levers are JITO private label, volume, device/OTC/nutrition mix, and data/logistics monetisation; management guided 10-11% in FY28-29 and said it is not formal guidance.

qa_highlights.question: Is the 30% growth guidance conservative, and how will costs scale?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said FY26 grew about 20%, average over the period is 33%, and it targets about 30% CAGR. Costs in new markets (Odisha, Jharkhand, Bihar, UP, Rajasthan) are funded from mature markets.

risks_watch: EBITDA loss widened in absolute terms (INR17.2 crore vs INR16 crore) and employee cost rose 12% QoQ ahead of new-market revenue; management says the investment will be recovered over 3-4 years.
JITO pricing is about one-third of branded medicine; revenue target cut to INR4,900 crore for FY30 and SastaSundar sharply reduced, so revenue mix is shifting.
Merger with Rohto Pharmaceuticals' subsidiary structure is pending SEBI observation letter, expected by end-December; NCLT approval would take 4-6 months.
RetailAir adoption is early (trial phase, launched about three months ago); next-quarter data was promised.
Management declined to quantify incremental fulfilment cost and small-distributor margin differences; disclosure limits on segment costs.
summary.management_tone: Confident on growth, unit economics and balance sheet, but defensive on profitability: management repeatedly asked investors to judge the business on its long-term framing and declined to give hard guidance on gross margin or EBITDA timing.

growth.why: Management reiterates ~30% compounded revenue growth over five years, but cut the FY29-30 revenue framing to INR4,900 crore from INR6,000 crore and the FY28-29 gross margin path to 10-11%, with growth backed by warehouse build-out (5.95 lakh sq ft, Udaipur first in ~18 months) and JITO private-label ramp, but no order book or firm capex figures.

quality.why: Revenue rose 59% YoY to INR489 crore, led by RetailerShakti (B2B) at INR429 crore (+60% YoY, +18% QoQ) across roughly 80,000 pharmacies, with SastaSundar up 39% YoY; the brief names no one-off gain, low base, or acquisition-driven item in the quarter.

rows.label: Margin expansion
rows.why: Gross margin at 8.3% (8.5-8.6% exit run-rate per management) with a 9-10% path in FY27-28 and 10-11% in FY28-29 driven by JITO private label, mix and data monetisation (~1% of GM), though management called it a range, not formal guidance, and EBITDA loss was still -3.5% of revenue with the absolute loss widening to INR17.2 crore.

rows.label: Capacity expansion / commissioning
rows.when: Q4 FY27 to Q2 FY28 (small warehouses ~6 months out)
rows.why: Smaller 20,000 sq ft warehouses in Ranchi, Patna and Bhubaneswar are in sign-up with operations about 6 months away, and Udaipur (80,000 sq ft) is first of the larger builds in about 18 months with plinth area complete.

rows.label: Volume growth
rows.why: RetailerShakti grew 60% YoY and 18% QoQ to INR429 crore across ~80,000 pharmacies, and JITO revenue is guided at INR6-10 crore next quarter, versus management's ~30% CAGR target.

rows.label: New capex announcement
rows.why: Fulfilment network is expanding into Odisha, Jharkhand, Bihar, UP and Rajasthan with ~5.95 lakh sq ft of additional space planned and the West Bengal 1.2 lakh sq ft build flagged as a 'raised' capex item, so further site commitments are likely; utilisation was not disclosed.

rows.label: Guidance upgrade
rows.why: Management cut the FY29-30 revenue framing to INR4,900 crore from INR6,000 crore and the SastaSundar growth budget to 50% from 100%, so the call points to lower, not higher, targets.

rows.label: Guidance downgrade
rows.why: FY29-30 revenue was already cut by about 18% (INR6,000 to INR4,900 crore) and employee cost rose 12% QoQ ahead of new-market revenue, while the merger completion depends on a SEBI observation letter expected by end-December.

rows.label: New product launch
rows.why: JITO private label has 52 franchise outlets live and 81 in pipeline with over 1,000 SKUs, plus RetailAir (launched ~3 months ago, next-quarter data promised) and device/OTC/nutrition mix levers.

rows.label: Merger completion pending SEBI observation letter
rows.when: letter expected by end-Dec 2026; NCLT 4-6 months
rows.why: Merger completion is tied to a SEBI observation letter expected by end-December, with NCLT approval taking a further 4-6 months, so completion may fall outside the 2-4 quarter window.

rows.label: JITO private-label gross margin ~60%
rows.why: JITO sales of INR2.2 crore in Q2 at about 60% gross margin, up ~170% QoQ, with INR6-10 crore guided next quarter, lifting blended gross margin even though JITO pricing is about one-third of branded medicine.

rows.label: Net working capital cut to 23 days
rows.why: Net working capital fell to 23 days from 28 days in Q1 (-18%), with inventory at 35 days, receivables at 2 days and payables at 13 days.
